text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government parties in Wifaq bloc are main winners in elections to professional bodies -- Moroccan chambers of agriculture, trade, craftsmen, maritime fishing.
- Ali Yata, secretary-general of opposition Progress and Socialism Party, hurt in car accident.
- Electricity grids of Morocco and Spain will be connected in September after successful tests in the Straits of Gibraltar.
- Customs officers in northern port town of Nador seize 109 kg (240 pounds) of gold in ingots and jewellery valued at about 13.1 million dirhams ($1.3 million).
- More than half a million Moroccan expatriates left from the Spanish port of Algeciras for summer holidays in Morocco.
- Algeria, which holds presidency of the five-nation Arab Maghreb Union, denies press report that a summit will be held at Tunis in November.
